tactical-board.subtitle: Grand Regent vs Demon King Piccolo

character-dossier-a.quote: BRING ME THE SKULLS OF THESE TRAITORS!
character-dossier-a.style: An absolute physical dominant — trained from birth in all manners of combat across centuries. Thragg doesn't need strategy. He walks in, crushes everything, and never lets up until the opponent falls apart.
character-dossier-a.advantage: Inhuman stamina and thermal endurance. Thragg fights at the same intensity for days — with his guts hanging out, without skin, on the surface of a star.
character-dossier-a.mentality: Cold, calculating tyrant. He doesn't kill from emotion — he kills because logic demands it. Every move is optimal, every victory calculated in advance.

character-dossier-b.quote: That's the problem with the human race. No respect... for the superior species.
character-dossier-b.style: No classical martial style. Piccolo fights through raw power, range control, and a broad technique arsenal rather than formal martial training.
character-dossier-b.advantage: Fast Namekian regeneration and very high offensive power. Piccolo hits harder than his size suggests and can return to battle after severe physical damage.
character-dossier-b.mentality: Cruel, manipulative Demon King. Arrogant but strategic — he knows the value of fear, knows when to press and when to wait for his opponent's mistake.

powers: Smart Atoms — adaptive biology resistant to star-level temperatures and extreme gravity. Superhuman strength, speed, endurance and flight.
tools: No specialized combat tools — Thragg fights purely with his own body.
weaknesses: Zero ranged attacks — no answer to energy attacks from a distance.
The Scourge Virus and Klaxus Plant can kill him.

powers: Planet level+ offensive power. Ki for precise ranged attacks.
tools: Ki blasts — ranged weapon without precedent in Thragg's entire arsenal.
Giant form and stretching limbs — strikes where Thragg least expects it.
weaknesses: Fighting at full power shortens his lifespan — cannot maintain peak form indefinitely.
Arrogance surrenders initiative; regeneration has limits, and critical head/brain damage can stop it.

a: Continues fighting with an exposed skull.
Dodges Space Racer's Infinity Ray and catches up with him.
b: Laughed off a Kamehameha from Goku.
22nd Budokai Goku stated that his speed didn't begin to compare to King Piccolo.
Creates powerful shockwaves with a swing of his hand.
Destroyed the pot he was trapped in with a glance.

final-summary.line_1: In Dragon Ball scaling, Ki amplifies the full combat profile: attack, speed, and body durability. On that logic, Piccolo starts ahead.
final-summary.line_2: Thragg has elite physicals and close-range pressure, but without comparable ranged power projection he does not control the flow of the matchup.
final-summary.line_3: Across the full fight, Piccolo has better damage economy, wider tactical options, and a more stable closing path.
final-summary.winner: Piccolo 10/10. Thragg has only surprise and brief initiative, but no reliable win condition.

battle-dynamics.label: Fight Scenario
battle-dynamics.phase_1: From the opening second, Piccolo holds the edge at every range: he can run the fight at distance or meet Thragg in direct exchanges.
battle-dynamics.phase_2: When Thragg closes in, Piccolo does not lose control. He accepts contact, lands heavier returns, and keeps Ki pressure active.
battle-dynamics.phase_3: The endgame is not tied to one method: Piccolo can close with ranged salvos or with a direct close-range finish.
battle-dynamics.analysis: This is not a one-path matchup. Piccolo wins both through field control and through raw exchange power.

fight-simulation.label: Fight Scenario
fight-simulation.opening: From the start, Piccolo can run either path: sustained ranged Ki pressure or hard close-range exchanges.
fight-simulation.mid_fight: Thragg tries to force his preferred rhythm, but Piccolo answers in both ranges and keeps initiative.
fight-simulation.late_fight: As the fight extends, every route leads to the same result: Piccolo's advantage becomes clearer.
fight-simulation.end_condition: Piccolo closes the fight by any method — long range, mid range, or clinch.
fight-simulation.phase_1_event: Thragg comes forward aggressively, but Piccolo immediately shows he can punish with both Ki fire and direct exchange power.
fight-simulation.phase_2_event: Even when Thragg gets in, Piccolo handles contact without losing tempo and lands the heavier return damage.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_a: Thragg drags it into a brawl — Piccolo still wins the exchanges.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_b: Thragg disengages under pressure — Piccolo retakes the Ki lane.
fight-simulation.phase_3_event: After breaking Thragg's rhythm, Piccolo chooses the finish: a controlled Ki end or a direct close-range shutdown.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_a: Piccolo closes with a short-range finishing series.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_b: Piccolo closes with a controlled Ki salvo.

direct-verdict.line_1: Ki scaling gives Piccolo the edge in the full combat profile: power, speed, and body durability.
direct-verdict.line_2: Thragg brings extreme physical pressure, but lacks the tools to take lasting control of the fight flow.
direct-verdict.line_3: At any range, Piccolo can close the fight on his own tempo — via Ki salvo or direct close-range finish.
